macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks slip as bond-market pressure persists; U.S. futures point lower
items.summary: Global shares edged lower on Monday as investors stayed focused on elevated Treasury yields, with S&P 500 futures down 0.2% and Nasdaq futures down 0.6% in early trade. Asian markets were broadly weaker, while Europe was slightly higher, and the 10-year U.S. yield remained around 4.71% near recent highs.

items.title: Wall Street ends last session mixed after recent record highs
items.summary: On Friday, the S&P 500 rose 0.4%, the Dow gained 1%, and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.4% after a stretch of volatile trading near all-time highs. Markets remain sensitive to bond yields and upcoming inflation data.

items.title: Treasury yield remains near multi-month highs as investors await Jackson Hole and PCE inflation data
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield was reported near 4.71%, still close to a 20-month high, with traders looking ahead to the Fed chair's Jackson Hole remarks and the July PCE inflation release. The 30-year yield also stayed elevated near its highest level since 2007.

items.title: Dollar hovers near multi-month lows amid debt and bond-buyback concerns
items.summary: Reuters reported the U.S. dollar trading near multi-month lows as investors reacted to Treasury plans to increase buybacks of longer-dated bonds. Markets are also waiting for policy signals from upcoming U.S. and Japanese central bank speeches.

items.title: Fed focus turns to Jackson Hole as inflation data and policy guidance loom
items.summary: Markets are bracing for the Fed's preferred inflation gauge and the Jackson Hole speech by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh for clues on the rate outlook. The combination of sticky inflation and high borrowing costs has kept policy expectations in sharp focus.

items.title: Gold rises above $4,650 as fiscal and rate-cut uncertainties support bullion
items.summary: Gold climbed to more than a three-month high, with spot prices around $4,637 and U.S. futures near $4,691, as the weaker dollar and fiscal concerns supported demand. Traders are positioning ahead of inflation data and Fed Chair remarks.

items.title: Alibaba drops after launching $10.2 billion share offering
items.summary: Alibaba shares fell about 8.5% in Hong Kong after the company launched a US$10.2 billion share offer, with investors also weighing concerns about returns from its heavy AI spending. The announcement was one of the biggest company-specific moves in the latest market session.

items.title: Samsung Electronics falls after record shareholder-return plan disappoints investors
items.summary: Samsung Electronics dropped more than 8% after unveiling a record US$79 billion shareholder-return plan that still fell short of some investors' expectations. The reaction underscored how AI-related capital allocation remains a key market theme.

items.title: Iran sanctions talk and oil weakness weigh on markets
items.summary: Oil prices eased as investors awaited details on threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran, while broader risk assets remained under pressure. Brent crude and U.S. benchmark crude were both lower in early trading.

items.title: Canada retail sales rise in June while trade tensions pressure the loonie
items.summary: Canadian retail sales rose 0.6% in June, but the Canadian dollar weakened as trade tensions with the U.S. intensified. The currency move came alongside broader market concern about tariffs and retaliation risks.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin nears $80,000 as crypto extends biggest 3-day rally since 2023
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 2% on Monday to just under $80,000, while ether gained about 2% to around $2,500, both reaching their highest levels in months. The move came amid a broad market rebound after crypto posted its biggest three-day rally since 2023.

items.title: Bitcoin’s weekly surge tops 22% as risk sentiment improves
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed nearly 22% over the past week and traded near $78,000, with ether also higher. Other major altcoins including BNB, Solana, Tron, Cardano, XRP, Hyperliquid, and Dogecoin posted smaller gains over the last 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto market rally triggers billions in short liquidations
items.summary: The latest surge in bitcoin led to roughly $2.74 billion in crypto short liquidations over 24 hours, one of the largest short-side wipeouts on record. The move reflects intense leverage unwinding as prices pushed sharply higher.

items.title: Bitcoin steadies above $77,000 as regulatory hopes support rebound
items.summary: Bitcoin held above $77,000 as traders reacted to improving regulatory expectations and broader market strength. Ether rose to about $2,458, while XRP was roughly flat.

items.title: SEC proposes crypto exemption rules for fundraising startups
items.summary: The SEC proposed capital-raising exemption rules for crypto startups, a notable regulatory development for the sector. The same market recap also noted fresh activity around Polymarket, Kalshi, and other crypto infrastructure projects.

items.title: EU weighs whether DeFi lending should fall under MiCA
items.summary: The European Commission is considering whether decentralized finance lending should be brought under the MiCA framework. A consultation running through September 30 is focused on identifying responsible parties and practical controls.

items.title: CFTC may regulate crypto markets even without the CLARITY Act
items.summary: CFTC Chair Mike Selig said the agency could create crypto market rules on its own if the CLARITY Act remains blocked. He said the agency could still develop specialized rules for trading platforms.

items.title: Term Finance reports major DeFi exploit tied to governance flaw
items.summary: Term Finance disclosed a governance vulnerability affecting its Term Vaults, with CertiK estimating losses at around $8.5 million. The investigation is still ongoing.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI CEO warns about concentration of AI power
items.summary: Sam Altman said he is concerned that AI could end up controlled by a small number of companies, models, or individuals, and argued that users should have deeper control over how the technology shapes the future.

items.title: Mystery model “Ox Alpha” surges across developer tools
items.summary: Several reports say an unidentified model called Ox Alpha has rapidly gained attention among developers and entered real-world coding and agent workflows, with some sources describing it as a reasoning model optimized for sustained production use.

items.title: Alibaba’s Wan 3.0 video model reportedly launches
items.summary: Reports from Chinese AI outlets say Alibaba Cloud’s Wan 3.0 video generation model is now live, with one report claiming it can generate up to 30 seconds of video per request.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly cuts API prices for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: A Japanese AI news roundup says OpenAI announced temporary promotional pricing for its GPT-5.6 Sol API model, lowering input-token costs by 20% and output-token costs by 33% through at least late November.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly pursues $6 billion Poolside deal for open-weight model
items.summary: A Yahoo Finance report says Nvidia is making a major push into foundation models through a multibillion-dollar partnership with Poolside to build a powerful open-weight AI system aimed at competing with leading frontier labs.

items.title: Murf AI launches Falcon 2 text-to-speech model
items.summary: A technology roundup reports that Murf AI has launched Falcon 2, a new text-to-speech model focused on more human-like voices at lower cost and faster speed.

items.title: AI infrastructure and chip costs dominate industry conversation
items.summary: Multiple reports highlight rising attention on AI infrastructure, including data-center buildouts, compute supply constraints, and higher AI-server prices tied to memory shortages and hardware demand.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass confirms June 2025 Wave 1 lineup
items.summary: Microsoft has revealed the first wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass in June 2025, ahead of the Xbox Games Showcase. The announcement is among the day’s notable release-related updates.

items.title: Helldivers 2 reveals new 'Force of Law' Warbond
items.summary: Arrowhead has announced a new Force of Law Warbond for Helldivers 2, giving players another upcoming content drop for the cooperative shooter.

items.title: Final Fantasy Tactics Collector's Box does not include the game
items.summary: Square Enix has unveiled a Collector's Box for Final Fantasy Tactics: The Ivalice Chronicles, but the bundle is being sold without a copy of the game. That detail has made the announcement especially notable among current gaming news.

items.title: Riot fighting game 2XKO is reportedly ending development
items.summary: VGC reports that Riot's fighting game 2XKO is officially ending development, making it one of the biggest industry-shift stories in the current news cycle.

items.title: Nintendo continues crackdown on Switch emulator repositories
items.summary: Nintendo has reportedly removed 400 more Switch emulator repositories from GitHub as part of its ongoing anti-piracy efforts. The move highlights the company’s continued legal and platform enforcement strategy.

items.title: Take-Two seeks records after apparent GTA VI hacker breach
items.summary: Reports say Take-Two is pursuing records after an apparent hacker breach tied to Grand Theft Auto VI material surfaced online. The incident is being treated as a major security and industry issue.

items.title: GTA VI leak fallout spreads across the industry
items.summary: Coverage in multiple outlets says the GTA VI leak saga has escalated, with legal pressure reportedly widening to major platforms and the broader publishing ecosystem. The story remains one of the most watched developments in gaming today.

items.title: EA shuts down more NHL servers
items.summary: ETtoday reports that EA has closed the servers for NHL 22 and NHL 23, adding to the growing list of older games being taken offline. The shutdown is part of a broader service-lifecycle trend in live gaming.

items.title: The Duskbloods network test hits login issues
items.summary: ETtoday says The Duskbloods' first network test was disrupted because players could not log in, forcing an official cancellation of the session. The issue has made the game one of the day's most discussed release-related headlines.

items.title: EA being acquired for $55 billion and going private
items.summary: Game Informer highlights a major industry development: Electronic Arts is being acquired for $55 billion and will go private. If completed, the deal would be one of the largest gaming industry transactions in recent memory.

items.title: Silent Hill f sells 1 million copies in under a week
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Silent Hill f has surpassed 1 million copies sold in less than a week. The sales milestone makes it one of the strongest launch stories in the current news cycle.

items.title: Star Wars Zero Company set for August 27 release
items.summary: AllKeyShop says Electronic Arts and Bit Reactor will launch STAR WARS Zero Company on August 27, 2026. The turn-based tactics game is one of the notable upcoming releases highlighted in current gaming coverage.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Alibaba shares plunge after $10.2 billion placement to fund AI push
items.summary: Alibaba announced a Hong Kong share placement worth about $10.2 billion to finance AI chips, infrastructure, and model development, and its stock fell sharply after the news. The move is one of the largest capital raises in the sector this week.

items.title: Visa to acquire fraud-intelligence firm BioCatch for $2.4 billion
items.summary: Visa said it will buy BioCatch, a company focused on fraud intelligence and behavioral biometrics, in a deal valued at $2.4 billion. The acquisition expands Visa’s security and risk-management capabilities in digital payments.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly consolidates consumer and business Copilot into one app
items.summary: A new Microsoft Copilot app is reported to combine consumer and workplace experiences, letting users switch between personal and work accounts in one place. The change also appears to streamline access to Microsoft 365 tools while retiring some older features.

items.title: Motorola launches Moto G Max in India
items.summary: Motorola has launched the Moto G Max in India with a 6.72-inch 120Hz display, Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 processor, 50MP main camera, and a 7,000mAh battery. The phone is positioned as a battery-heavy midrange model.

items.title: SK Hynix unveils next-generation high-bandwidth memory packaging
items.summary: SK Hynix introduced a new HBM packaging approach with Intel EMIB at Hot Chips 2026, aimed at boosting bandwidth for AI accelerators and data-center GPUs. The company said volume production is expected in 2027.

items.title: Sony PlayStation terms email sparks global player backlash
items.summary: Sony’s email about updated PlayStation terms of service has triggered protests from users concerned about the shift toward digital-only ownership. The reaction reflects broader tension over licensing versus ownership in gaming.

items.title: Rockstar subpoenas Microsoft and Discord over GTA 6 leaks
items.summary: Rockstar Games has reportedly taken legal action by subpoenaing Microsoft and Discord in connection with major GTA 6 leaks. The case highlights the escalating security and leak-prevention issues around blockbuster game development.
